contract: one authored script read whole with ass_read_memory, or one stream fixture run on a track from ass_new_track as ass-parse-chunks runs it (codec private, packets through ass_process_chunk with ReadOrder deduplication, flushes and ass_prune_events), configured as a player embeds libass 0.17.5: a library with font extraction on and the fixture's font files given to ass_add_font in order, a renderer with frame and storage size set (the storage smaller than the frame: 1280x720 on 1920x1080, and 720x576 on 1280x720, whose pixel aspect is not 1), ASS_HINTING_NONE, ass_set_cache_limits(renderer, 1000, 24), libass's plain C bitmap engine on every host, and ass_set_fonts with the fixture's default font file and family and ASS_FONTPROVIDER_NONE
frames rendered with ass_render_frame at the fixture's times: a whole script's ;@frames, a stream's @frames commands where they stand among its packets and prunes

every frame folds its time, the change ass_render_frame reports (0, 1 or 2, as ass_detect_change computes it) and its image count, then every image its type, position, width, height and colour and every row of its alpha bytes, in libass's list order; the box add_background draws behind a BorderStyle 4 event, whose type libass leaves uninitialised, is told by its own buffer (the only one ass_render.c allocates aligned to one byte, which ass_aligned_alloc never aligns to the engine's rows, tested even where shift_event has moved the bitmap down it) and has type 3, one past IMAGE_TYPE_SHADOW, which the candidate gives its background box; packets count images and bytes their alpha bytes

the fixture and its attached font files are read before each timed and memory operation, which, as a player does, creates the library, hands it the attached fonts (ass_add_font copies them; the candidate copies them into its budget), opens the default font file (libass through FreeType; the candidate reads it), creates the renderer, reads the script or runs the stream and renders every frame; the timed span ends before the track, renderer and library are freed, on both sides, so neither times the teardown that releases its caches

timing and memory are measured against libass-player-native, libass.a linked as a player links it with none of its sources compiled into the worker; the parity reference libass-ass-native compiles libass's rendering, drawing and parsing sources with checks that note the conversions C leaves to the target, and is never timed or measured
